source.title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Determine the best possible universal lower bound on the spanning ratio of plane geometric graphs. More specifically, does there exist a real number t greater than √2.005367532 and a finite planar point set P such that every triangulation of P has spanning ratio at least t?
accepted.context_brief: Lower bound for plane spanning ratio

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1. What is the best lower bound on the spanning ratio of plane geometric graphs? Specifically, is there a t > √2.005367532 and a point set P, such that every triangulation of P has spanning ratio at least t?

accepted.question_text: Determine the best possible upper bound on the worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation of a planar point set. In addition, decide whether one can prove a strictly smaller worst-case upper bound when the input points are in convex position.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2. What is the best upper bound on the spanning ratio of the Delaunay triangulation? Can one prove a smaller upper bound on the spanning ratio for points in convex position?

accepted.question_text: Determine the best possible lower bound on the worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation. In particular, can one construct a planar point set whose Delaunay triangulation has spanning ratio strictly greater than 1.5932, and can one do so with the points restricted to convex position so that the spanning ratio is strictly greater than 1.581?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3. What is the best lower bound on the worst-case spanning ratio of the Delaunay triangulation? Can one construct a point set such that the spanning ratio of its Delaunay triangulation is strictly greater than 1.5932? For points in convex position, can one construct a point set such that the spanning ratio is strictly greater than 1.581?

accepted.question_text: Determine the best possible universal upper bound on the spanning ratio of a plane geometric graph on a finite planar point set.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4. What is the best upper bound on the spanning ratio of a plane graph? The best that is currently known is an upper bound of 1.998.

accepted.question_text: Given a finite planar point set, determine whether computing a plane geometric graph on that point set whose spanning ratio is minimum among all plane geometric graphs on the same vertex set is NP-hard.
accepted.context_brief: Complexity of minimum spanning ratio graph

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5. Is computing the plane graph of minimum spanning ratio for a given point set an NP-hard problem?

accepted.question_text: Given a finite planar point set, determine whether computing a plane spanning tree whose spanning ratio is minimum among all plane spanning trees on that point set is NP-hard.
accepted.context_brief: Complexity of minimum spanning ratio tree

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6. Is computing the plane spanning tree of minimum spanning ratio for a given point set an NP-hard problem?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a plane geometric graph on a finite planar point set has the α-diamond property for some fixed α and also has the d-good polygon property for some fixed d ≥ 1. Can the known general upper bound 8d(π − α)^2/(α^2 sin^2(α/4)) on its spanning ratio be improved to a strictly smaller bound?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7. Can the spanning ratio for plane graphs with the α-diamond property and the d-good polygon property be improved? Specifically, can one show that the spanning ratio is strictly less than 8d(π − α)^2/(α^2 sin^2(α/4))?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the guaranteed α-value in the α-diamond-property analysis of greedy triangulations can be improved beyond π/6.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8. Is the α-value for greedy triangulations greater than π/6?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the guaranteed α-value in the α-diamond-property analysis of minimum-weight triangulations can be improved beyond π/8.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9. Is the α-value for minimum weight triangulations greater than π/8?

accepted.question_text: For β-skeletons with parameter β in the interval [1, 2], determine whether one can prove a stronger lower bound on the spanning ratio that depends explicitly on β.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10. For the range β ∈ [1, 2], is there a stronger lower bound of the spanning ratio that depends on β?

accepted.question_text: For β-skeletons with parameter β in the interval [1, 2], determine whether the known upper bound (n−1)^γ on the spanning ratio, where γ = 1 − log2(√(2/β)), is tight for all β in that range.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11. For the range β ∈ [1, 2], is the upper bound on the spanning ratio of (n−1)^γ, where γ = 1 − log2(√(2/β)), tight? It is tight for the GG, where β = 1 and RNG, where β = 2.

accepted.question_text: For relaxed Gabriel graphs RGGβ(P) = BSKELβ(P) ∩ DT(P) with β in [0, 1], determine whether the known asymptotic upper and lower bounds on the spanning ratio are tight.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 12. Are these upper and lower bounds tight?

accepted.question_text: Determine the smallest possible maximum degree of a plane spanner that is required to be a subgraph of the standard Euclidean Delaunay triangulation of the input point set.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13. What is the smallest maximum degree that can be achieved for plane spanners that are subgraphs of the standard Delaunay triangulation?

accepted.question_text: Determine the smallest possible maximum degree that always suffices to construct a plane spanner on an arbitrary finite planar point set.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 14. What is the smallest maximum degree that can be achieved for plane spanners?

accepted.question_text: Decide whether the planarity requirement forces a worst-case lower bound on maximum degree that is strictly larger than 3 for geometric spanners. Equivalently, for every real t > 1, must there exist a planar point set P such that every plane degree-3 spanning graph on P has spanning ratio greater than t?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15. With the constraint of constructing a plane spanner, is there a lower bound on the maximum degree that is greater than 3? That is, can we show the following: For every real number t > 1, there exists a set P of points, such that every plane degree-3 spanning graph of P has spanning ratio greater than t.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the known bounds for constructing plane spanners that simultaneously have low total weight and bounded maximum degree are tight.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 16. Are these bounds tight?

accepted.question_text: For finite planar point sets, improve the dependence on ε in constructions of plane Steiner (1 + ε)-spanners; in particular, can one obtain such spanners using asymptotically fewer Steiner points than the O(n/ε^4) bound described in the paper?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 17. Can the dependence on ε in the solution sketched above be improved?

accepted.question_text: Determine the smallest real number t such that every finite planar point set has dilation at most t when dilation is defined as the infimum, over all plane graphs with only finitely many added Steiner vertices, of the graph’s spanning ratio on all points of the set.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 18. What is the smallest value of t such that every finite set of points in the plane has dilation at most t? It is known that 1.00157 ≤ t ≤ 1.1247.

accepted.question_text: Determine the exact dilation of the five vertices of a regular pentagon in the plane.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 19. What is the dilation of the vertices of a regular 5-gon? It is known that this dilation is at most 1.02046; see [34].

accepted.question_text: Determine the smallest real number t such that every finite planar point set has geometric dilation at most t, where geometric dilation takes the supremum over all pairs of points lying on the graph’s edges or vertices rather than only over original input vertices.
accepted.context_brief: Geometric dilation of planar point sets

evidence.quote: Open Problem 20. What is the smallest value of t such that every finite set of points in the plane has geometric dilation at most t? It is known that (1 + 10−11)π/2 ≤ t ≤ 1.678.

accepted.question_text: In the constrained visibility-graph setting, where one is given a finite point set P and a noncrossing set L of constrained line segments and studies plane constrained spanners of the visibility graph VIS(P, L), determine the constrained analogues of the open questions from the unconstrained plane-spanner setting, since the constrained model generalizes the unconstrained one.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 21. Essentially, all of the questions that are open in the unconstrained setting are also open in the constrained setting since the constrained setting is a generalization of the unconstrained one.

accepted.question_text: For a connected unit-disk graph UDG(P) modeling a wireless ad hoc network on a planar point set P, reduce the total number of broadcast messages needed by a local distributed algorithm to compute a plane local spanner of UDG(P).

evidence.quote: Open Problem 22. Can one reduce the total number of messages in order to compute a plane local spanner of UDG(P)?
